reason: Hypothesis A proposes a physically sound mechanism (rare-earth dopant segregation forming a protective oxide/intermetallic barrier) grounded in cited evidence on Y/Hf co-doping for high-temperature corrosion resistance, and it specifies a clear, testable experiment with a defined baseline and falsification rule. Hypothesis B lacks supporting evidence, invents a precise 30% improvement without justification, and relies on a chromium coating that may not be stable or effective in molten aluminum at 660°C, making it less grounded and less likely to address the limitation substantively.
